correctness.rationale: For unordered pairs of disjoint closed graph cells of W=K1*C5, direct independent graph enumeration confirms 15 vertex pairs, 40 nonincident vertex-edge pairs and 20 disjoint edge pairs; these are all cells of the finite two-particle cubical model. Full chains of its face poset (not chains of cell-orbit labels) give an admissible barycentric quotient triangulation since dimension-distinct flag vertices preclude inversions. The attached verify.py constructs every flag, finite D5 subgroup, canonical flag orbit and Burnside orbit count; the exact orbit flag cell counts are respectively (75,240,160), (15,48,32), (41,122,80), (11,26,16) for 1,C5,C2,D5. Its explicit free-face search tests unique surviving incidence before each elementary collapse, collapsing every two-cell and leaving connected one-dimensional graphs (23,28), (7,8), (11,12), (1,0). Each collapse preserves integral homotopy and yields beta1=6,2,2,0. All subgroup conjugacy classes (1,2,5,10) are exhausted. This is a finite constructive proof when the enumerator and certificates are executed; the full algorithm and incidence guards were inspected, and wheel cubical base counts independently recomputed; the exhaustive collapse was not independently replayed in this run.
